## Simple explanation

PyTorch is a toolkit for writing programs that learn from data. It supplies
multidimensional arrays, operations that can run on CPUs or GPUs, and tools
that calculate how model parameters should change during training.

## Technical explanation

PyTorch is an open-source machine-learning framework. Its tensor library
provides shape-aware numerical operations, while autograd records operations
and computes derivatives for gradient-based learning. `torch.nn` provides
modules and losses, and `torch.optim` provides parameter-update algorithms.

## Why it matters in AI engineering

The framework is widely used to prototype and train neural networks, build
custom learning systems, and run models in production. Its Python interface
lets engineers combine model code with the broader Python data and deployment
ecosystem.

## How it works

An engineer defines a model from tensor operations, computes a prediction and
loss, then asks autograd to calculate gradients. An optimizer uses those
gradients to update parameters; devices and distributed tools can scale the
computation.

## Practical example

For image classification, a PyTorch model maps a batch of image tensors to
class scores. A training step compares those scores with labels, calls
`loss.backward()`, updates the model with an optimizer, and clears gradients
before the next step.

## Common misconceptions

- PyTorch does not choose a good model, dataset, or objective automatically.
- Moving tensors to a GPU does not guarantee a speedup; small workloads can
  spend more time on transfer and launch overhead.
